newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori says rebel siege isolated event.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says rebel siege isolated event.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori said on Thursday the hostage crisis in Lima was an isolated event that would not affect Peru's economic recovery.
In a speech, he condemned Marxist guerrillas holding hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence as terrorists who had chosen a mistaken path of violence to resolve Peru's social problems.

The Dec. 17 takeover of the residence was "an isolated event that is not going to upset the Peruvian economy," Fujimori said in a 15-minute speech at Peru's Palace of Justice, only his second since the crisis started.
"They (the guerrillas) cannot say that by destroying factories, bridges and by chasing away investors and tourists that poverty is going to be reduced," he added.
Fujimori gave no clues on his strategy to tackle the siege. He described 1996 as "a very difficult year," but emphasised that his government would spend 1997 working for "peace and employment."

The takeover of the Japanese embassy residence by members of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) presented Fujimori with his toughest challenge in six years in office. The guerrillas, who initially held more than 500 hostages, were still holding 74 men on Thursday after a series of releases.
